source: Anderson, Verhoef, Zohrehvand (2026) Recipes for Creativity: Iterative Generation and Evaluation in LLMs
finding: Generate-then-select (FunSearch loop) for recipes. More iterations did not raise creativity. A smaller in-loop selector gave higher creativity scores than a larger one.
numbers: Mean TTCT-style creativity at 5/15/30 iterations: 3.921/3.835/3.927 vs human reference 3.638 (30 Pillsbury recipes). One iteration: in-loop score 4.00 vs 4.71 with search, final creativity about 4.1 both. Higher temperature gave no significant gain on any dimension; lower temperature cut originality.
quote: evaluator design is a first-order design variable in subjective creative search
limits: Pilot. LLM judges, not humans. No equal-token control. Selector criteria were not creativity. Human set was 30 recipes without stories.
agent_relevance: A separate evaluate step helps only if the selector rewards the right thing. A stricter or larger selector can reduce novelty. Partial answer to gaps 1 and 7.

source: MUTATE and ReDNA (2026) Beyond One Path: Evaluating and Enhancing Divergent Thinking in Interactive LLM Agents
finding: Frontier agents under immediate goal pressure fixate on obvious actions. ReDNA first proposes candidates with no goal or failure context, then reintroduces the constraints to pick one. It beat Self-Refine and EscapeAgent.
numbers: GPT-5.4 ablation (56 trials): Base 27/56 paths (48.2%), Reflect-only 33/56 (58.9%), full ReDNA 38/56 (67.9%). Elaboration 2.73 to 3.26. AUT transfer (GPT-5.4, T=0.7, 3 runs): originality 2.91 to 3.77 (+0.86), elaboration 4.36 to 4.97 (+0.61).
quote: separates unconstrained divergent candidate generation from convergent constraint selection
limits: ReDNA uses extra calls, so it is not equal-token. LLM-scored AUT. Ten hand-made scenarios, one ablation model.
agent_relevance: Closest direct test of O4 found: a loose generate pass followed by a constrained select pass raises originality, and goal-path success also rises. Needs an equal-token rerun.

source: Gerver, Griffin, Dennis, Beaty (2023) Memory and creativity: a meta-analytic examination (Psychon Bull Rev)
finding: Memory predicts creativity modestly. Semantic memory is the strongest link. Working memory is weaker. No sign of publication bias.
numbers: 525 effect sizes, 79 studies, N = 12,846, overall r = .19. By type: semantic .25, working memory .17, episodic .16, short-term .15 (Q = 33.56, p < .0001). Modified Egger test b = -0.11, se 0.37, p = .76. Without 56 unpublished effect sizes r = .19, 95% CI .16 to .22.
limits: All memory types pooled in the headline. Working memory more tied to convergent than divergent thinking. Correlational.
agent_relevance: Control capacity (working memory) is a small contributor; stored knowledge matters more. Do not buy originality with extra working context alone.

source: Chen et al. (2024) A meta-analysis of the effects of tDCS on creative thinking (Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts)
finding: Small positive effect of anodal tDCS on creativity, none for cathodal. Overall gain was for convergent, not divergent, thinking. Left DLPFC anodal helped both. Left IFG anodal lowered performance.
numbers: 32 studies, 125 effect sizes, 1,538 participants. Effect sizes g and bias tests not shown on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only; g values and publication-bias results not seen. Gap 2 stays partly open for this paper.
agent_relevance: More control at left prefrontal sites helped, which cuts against a simple 'less control is better' story.

source: Chan, Cho, Lambon Ralph, Robinson (2025) Cross-domain meta-analysis of tDCS studies on creative thought (bioRxiv preprint)
finding: Only anodal left lateral frontal stimulation consistently helped creativity and general cognitive control mechanisms. Funnel plots showed no obvious publication bias (visual check only).
numbers: 20 creativity + 152 cognitive studies, 591 effect sizes. Left lateral frontal anodal: divergent d = .540, 95% CI [.00004, 1.08], p = .0498; convergent d = .401, CI [.026, .776], p = .036. Mean d across creativity studies 0.25; about 98 participants (49 per group) needed for 80% power. I2 for creativity montages < 1% to 67%.
quote: Visual inspection of funnel plots did not reveal apparent publication bias
limits: Preprint. Visual funnel check only, no Egger or trim-and-fill. 83% of creativity effect sizes from verbal semantic tasks. Divergent CI touches zero.
agent_relevance: Prefrontal control is a cornerstone of idea generation, not only a brake. Supports keeping a control stage in the scaffold.

source: Chrysikou et al. (2021) Differential effects of tDCS over left and right ventrolateral PFC on ideational fluency (Scientific Reports)
finding: Same-lab replication and extension of the 2013 cathodal left PFC result across four experiments and twelve montages. Left ventrolateral PFC inhibition sped and increased idea fluency; originality (semantic distance) did not change.
numbers: 246 participants over 4 experiments (Exp 1 N = 60, Exp 4 N = 66 among them). Sample size set from the prior medium-to-large effect, raised about 20%. Fluency by voice-onset RT; weaker for number of responses.
limits: Same lab. No preregistration found in the text. Small groups per condition. The originality effect was not reproduced.
agent_relevance: Loosened control helps volume of ideas, not distance from the obvious. So relaxation (O4) may widen the pool but needs a separate novelty push.

source: Rosen et al. (2016) Anodal tDCS to right DLPFC facilitates novice jazz improvisers but hinders experts (Front Hum Neurosci)
finding: No main effect of anodal or cathodal stimulation. Interaction with expertise: helped less experienced pianists, hurt more experienced. Two searches found no direct replication.
numbers: N = 17 as recorded in earlier evidence; 1.5 mA for 15 min; ratings by jazz experts.
limits: Seen here only as search result text. Single small study.
agent_relevance: Expertise-dependent relaxation remains a hypothesis, not a replicated finding.

source: Khalil et al. (2023) Individual differences and creative ideation: neuromodulatory signatures of mindset and response inhibition (Front Neurosci)
finding: Individual traits moderate tDCS effects on idea generation. Mindset moderated the effect of inferior frontal stimulation on fluency and flexibility, not originality, with opposite sign for left versus right IFG.
numbers: N = 40 (R+L- n = 19; R-L+ n = 21), AUT fluency, originality, flexibility, go/no-go before and after.
limits: Small. Inferior frontal gyrus, not DLPFC. Not an expertise test. No sham group.
agent_relevance: Only partial support for a baseline-dependent rule (gap 3): the sign of the effect depends on person traits, so one fixed relaxation setting is risky.

source: Luyten and van der Schaar (2026) The Reasoning-Creativity Trade-off: Toward Creativity-Driven Problem Solving
finding: Theory paper. Correctness-only training (STaR, GRPO, DPO) is argued to decay the diversity of reasoning paths. Entropy bonuses and related designs can keep a diverse policy.
numbers: Theorems and recipes; no human-rated creativity numbers read.
limits: Mostly theory. Skimmed; empirical sections not checked for numbers.
agent_relevance: Gives a mechanism for why reasoning-trained models may be narrower. Treat as a mechanism claim, not a measured effect.

source: Output diversity collapse in Olmo 3 post-training lineages (2026) Where does output diversity collapse in post-training?
finding: Diversity collapse is set by training data, not by the chain-of-thought format. Turning off CoT at inference lowers hard-task accuracy but does not restore diversity.
numbers: Think-SFT loses 62% of base diversity on average (24% more than Instruct). 15 tasks, four diversity metrics. CoT suppression: accuracy falls on hard tasks (geometry -32%), answer diversity unchanged. Think models keep more correct-answer diversity than Instruct.
limits: One model family (Olmo 3). Verifiable and open tasks mixed.
agent_relevance: At inference, a visible reasoning step is not what narrows ideas; the trained weights are. Switching reasoning off will not buy originality.

source: LLMs Exhibit Significantly Lower Uncertainty in Creative Writing Than Professional Writers (2026)
finding: Instruction-tuned and reasoning ('thinking') variants widen the gap to human uncertainty compared with base models. More reasoning compute did little to recover it. Higher uncertainty correlates weakly with writing quality.
numbers: 28 LLMs, 3 datasets. Human continuations 2 to 4 times higher entropy. Spearman |rho| 0.07 to 0.11 between uncertainty and a quality reward-model score. PMI gap 25 to 30% wider for creative than functional domains.
limits: Quality from a reward model, not people. Open-weight models. Correlational.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for gap 6: reasoning-mode training goes with less spread in creative writing.

source: A Cognitive Framework for Idea Diversity in Large Language Models (2026)
finding: Chain-of-thought prompting reduces fixation in LLM ideation and raises diversity. It did not help humans. Personas plus CoT gave the most diverse idea sets.
numbers: Fixation slope (unique categories) default 1.023 vs CoT 1.354 (p < .001); human 1.020 vs human CoT 1.035 (p = .70). 83 sessions per condition: unique combinations default LLM 85, CoT 152, humans 196, personas+CoT 240. In a second model run CoT narrowed first-idea diversity (7.11 vs 9.14, p < .001).
limits: Product ideation; model-dependent (CoT narrowed first-idea diversity in the second run). Tokens not equated.
agent_relevance: Reasoning prompts can fight fixation, so reasoning does not always narrow. Prompted CoT and reasoning-trained models are different things.

source: Wong, Goes, Volpe, Mann (2026) How Context Injection Shapes Creativity in LLM-Generated Alternative Uses (ICCC26 short paper)
finding: Injecting unrelated or random context into AUT prompts shifts outputs. Random context maximised judged novelty; unrelated context raised category flexibility; related context kept value.
numbers: 4 open-weight LLMs, 6 objects, 20 uses per object-condition. Flexibility gain largest for unrelated context (10.117 vs 3.889 for the comparison condition). No human judges.
quote: context type determines the direction of measured output change rather than providing a uniform creativity boost
limits: LLM-judged proxies, LLM-generated snippets, no equal-token or human check. Not a test of attention leakiness itself.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 partly answered: some irrelevant material lifts novelty, but the effect is metric-specific and quality is not shown.

source: Does Less Hallucination Mean Less Creativity? An Empirical Investigation in LLMs (2025)
finding: Hallucination-reduction methods change divergent creativity in opposite directions. Chain of Verification raised it, DoLa layer contrasting lowered it, RAG had minimal effect.
numbers: LLaMA, Qwen, Mistral, 1B to 70B parameters, NeoCoder and CS4 benchmarks. Effect sizes not read (abstract only).
agent_relevance: A verification-style control step (CoVe) did not kill divergent output, so a check stage and divergence can coexist.

source: CreativityPrism (2025) A Cross-Domain Evaluation Framework for LLM Creativity
finding: Across 17 LLMs, frontier models lead in creative writing and logical reasoning but not in divergent thinking. Performance in one creativity dimension rarely carries to another.
numbers: 8 tasks, 3 domains. Frontier lead about 0.10 (15%) over local open models in writing and reasoning; no significant lead in divergent thinking. Novelty metrics show weak or negative correlation with other metrics.
limits: Abstract only. Does not include executive-function task scores.
agent_relevance: Bears on gap 5: skill in one creativity dimension does not travel to another, so a control-task score is unlikely to predict originality without a direct test.

source: Search for LLM executive-function scores versus creativity (2026 search; Strong Memory, Weak Control 2504.02789 and human flanker/WCST study)
finding: Search found LLM executive-function batteries and human studies where inhibition predicts AUT originality, but no study joining the two across models.
numbers: Human comparator: attentional inhibition predicted AUT originality but not fluency or flexibility; flexibility predicted no AUT dimension.
limits: Absence of evidence from a limited search (one web search and arXiv queries).
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays open. Do not assume stronger Flanker or WCST scores mean more originality in a model.

source: CreativityNeuro (2026) Steering Language Model Weights to Improve Divergent Thinking and Reduce Mode Collapse
finding: Weight masks found by contrasting creative and non-creative prompts raise DAT but also hurt factual MMLU. Adding MMLU prompts to the protection set did not protect MMLU.
numbers: Six open models, 3B to 14B. Default masks: MMLU -3.13 pp on average (500 questions, 5 seeds). MMLU-protected masks: +1.33 more DAT percentile, MMLU a further -0.71 pp. No closed or larger models; no replication elsewhere.
quote: divergent thinking and factual reasoning are functionally entangled and non-separable in weight space
limits: Single source. Wanda-style importance may cause the entanglement. Only MMLU as correctness cost.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: no larger-model replication found; correctness cost beyond MMLU untested. Entanglement argues for stage separation in the prompt, not weight edits.

source: Chrysikou 2011 / 2013 matched-filter line: replication status search (2026)
finding: No preregistered replication of Chrysikou 2011 or the 2013 tDCS study was found. The nearest is the same lab's 2021 four-experiment extension (d06), which reproduced the fluency gain but not an originality gain.
numbers: 2021 paper: 246 participants, 12 montages; no preregistration statement found in text.
limits: Absence found by two web searches and one full-text read; a preregistered replication may exist unindexed.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open. Use the matched-filter idea as a design hypothesis, not a proven rule.
